verdict.rationale: For payment-card purchases, Skyfire documents cardholder consent that covers a merchant and an amount ceiling, plus user mandate collection, so card spending is bounded by documented approval. However, wallet-funded pay tokens can be created by the agent itself (via API/MCP) from a pre-funded wallet, and no human confirmation step is documented before that money moves. missing for 10: a documented human approval/confirmation step for wallet-based pay-token spending, configurable thresholds for what counts as 'sensitive' spending requiring approval, detail on how the mandate/consent UX works, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, sensitive agent spending requires my documented approval — a confirmation step, signed mandate, or per-purchase consent — before money moves

citations.quote: The agent/agent platform can never spend more than the cardholder approved.
Skyfire partners with all major credit card networks to allow tokenized card transactions and user mandate collection
A KYAPay token is a signed, interoperable credential that packages agent identity and payment intent into a verifiable envelope.
